issues.t: CVT shudder or surging
issues.sym: A shake or judder when pulling away or at light throttle, or the engine speed surging up and down while cruising.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a service bulletin (TSB-20-23-001, revised several times through 2024) for shudder and surge from the hydraulic pressure circuit in this CVT. Later bulletins added a CVT belt check procedure.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check the transmission against the bulletin. The CVT is covered by the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty for the original owner, so go to a dealer first.

issues.t: Check engine light and power loss from ignition coils
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rough or shaky idle, misfires, and the engine dropping into a low-power fail-safe mode.
issues.why: Mitsubishi found poor contact at the ignition coil terminals. Its bulletin TSB-22-16-001 tells dealers to replace the coils on all cylinders with improved parts.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Misfire codes (P0300-P0304) point to this bulletin; ask the dealer to replace all the coils with the countermeasure parts.

issues.t: Check engine light with cam timing codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0010-P0017, and in some cases a hard start or no-start.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released updated engine computer software for these camshaft timing codes and a no-start condition, and also has a procedure for replacing the oil control valve when it is at fault.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer whether the engine computer software update has been done before parts are replaced.

issues.t: Stalling or weak throttle in cold weather
issues.sym: The engine stalls soon after a cold start, or barely responds to the gas pedal at startup, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released engine computer reprogramming for cold-weather stalling and related check engine codes on early trucks.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the cold-weather engine software update has been done.

issues.t: Check engine light with speed limited
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0068 or P061A and the vehicle limiting its speed.
issues.why: Early engine computer software could set these codes incorrectly. Mitsubishi released reprogramming to fix it.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the code and apply the software update.

issues.t: Fuel smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A gasoline or oily smell inside the cabin from the vents while the engine runs, especially with recirculation off.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a bulletin for fuel odor coming through the HVAC vents and tested revised breather and vacuum hoses. Owners also report an oil and gas smell in the cabin and engine bay.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Have a dealer check for leaks and apply the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Coolant warning light from leaking hose
issues.sym: A low coolant warning light, a sweet smell, or coolant drips at the front of the engine.
issues.why: A coolant hose connection can leak at its clamp. Mitsubishi's fix is a new water hose and improved clamp.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and top up with the correct coolant. Have the hose and clamp replaced before it runs low and overheats.

issues.t: Rattle from exhaust manifold heat shield
issues.sym: A tinny rattle from the engine area at idle or certain engine speeds.
issues.why: The heat protector over the exhaust manifold can rattle. Mitsubishi's bulletin replaces the heat shield assembly.
issues.next: Have the heat shield checked. It's not dangerous but should be fixed so it doesn't come loose.

issues.t: Weak heat at idle or low speed
issues.sym: The heater blows only lukewarm air when idling or driving slowly in cold weather.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released new climate control software to improve heater output at idle and low speeds.
issues.next: Check that the coolant is full, then ask a dealer for the A/C control unit reprogramming.

issues.t: Noise from the heater blower
issues.sym: A buzzing, whirring or rattling noise from behind the dash whenever the fan is on.
issues.why: Mitsubishi published a fix for HVAC noise that happens when the blower motor runs.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the blower against the bulletin.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge or range display drops suddenly or shows the wrong level, and some owners have run out of gas.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released instrument cluster reprogramming for an inaccurate fuel level display. Owners have reported the range dropping to empty without warning.
issues.next: Fill up by the trip odometer until it's fixed, and ask a dealer for the instrument cluster update.

issues.t: Driver window or lock switch sticks or stops working
issues.sym: The driver's window won't go up or down, stops after the one-touch function is used, or the lock or window switches stick.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued bulletins for driver door lock and window switches that stick, and for the driver window switch becoming inoperable with the one-touch feature.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the window switch bulletins; the fix is usually a replacement switch.

issues.t: Front window rattle or chatter
issues.sym: The front door glass rattles or chatters, especially on rough roads or when partly open.
issues.why: Mitsubishi's bulletin replaces the front door window run channel to stop the noise.
issues.next: Have the window run channel replaced if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Glove box won't latch
issues.sym: The glove box won't stay closed or pops open.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a bulletin for a glove box locking mechanism that may not latch properly.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Driver seat slowly sinks
issues.sym: The manual driver seat gradually lowers over time on its own.
issues.why: Mitsubishi's bulletin replaces the manual seat height adjustment levers when the driver seat slowly drops.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the height adjustment levers.

issues.t: Pulls to one side or steering wheel off-center
issues.sym: The SUV drifts or pulls left or right on a straight road, or the steering wheel sits crooked when driving straight.
issues.why: Mitsubishi has several notices on alignment checks for pulling or an off-center wheel, plus a correction to the front toe-in setting and steering computer reprogramming for early trucks.
issues.next: Check tire pressures first, then have a four-wheel alignment done to Mitsubishi's current specs.

issues.t: Liftgate won't stay open
issues.sym: The rear liftgate drifts down or won't stay up on its own.
issues.why: The liftgate gas springs can lose force. Mitsubishi published how to check their opening force and when to replace them.
issues.next: Don't rely on a weak liftgate to stay up. Have both gas springs replaced.

issues.t: Vibration from out-of-balance wheels on new vehicles
issues.sym: A shake in the steering wheel or seat at highway speeds on a new or nearly new vehicle.
issues.why: Mitsubishi opened an investigation into wheels found out of balance during pre-delivery inspection or soon after delivery, and added the 2022 Eclipse Cross to it.
issues.next: Have the wheels re-balanced; ask the dealer to do it under warranty.

issues.t: Smartphone link, CarPlay or Android Auto glitches
issues.sym: Apple CarPlay or Android Auto won't connect, drops out, or the screen doesn't respond to taps.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released several software updates for the Smartphone Link Display Audio unit and a notice about CarPlay not responding after an iPhone update. Owners have also reported Android Auto failures.
issues.next: Update your phone, try a different cable, and ask a dealer to update the radio software.

issues.t: Blind spot warning acts up
issues.sym: The blind spot warning gives false alerts, misses vehicles, or shows a system warning.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released gateway computer reprogramming for the blind spot warning system.
issues.next: Keep checking mirrors and over your shoulder, and ask a dealer for the gateway software update.

issues.t: Automatic headlights stay on in daylight
issues.sym: With the switch on AUTO, the headlights stay on even in bright conditions.
issues.why: Mitsubishi released body control computer (ETACS) reprogramming to fix this.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the ETACS software update.

issues.t: Collision mitigation brakes longer than needed (recall)
issues.sym: The automatic braking system keeps braking after a pedestrian is no longer detected, causing sudden, hard slowing.
issues.why: Incorrect software in the Forward Collision Mitigation computer (NHTSA campaign 18V620).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; the dealer reprograms the system for free.

issues.t: Emergency braking, ABS or stability control may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving, but automatic emergency braking, ABS, stability control or Brake Auto Hold may not step in when needed.
issues.why: The brake hydraulic unit computer could have incorrect software on models with adaptive cruise or the electric parking brake (NHTSA campaign 18V621).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; the dealer updates the software for free.
